exclusions: all document genres forced into IMRaD

sources.title: Recommendations: Preparing a Manuscript for Submission to a Medical Journal
sources.author: International Committee of Medical Journal Editors
sources.accessScope: General Principles, Reporting Guidelines, and Introduction–Discussion sections; not every linked reporting standard. Recommendations index: https://www.icmje.org/recommendations/ .
sources.rights: ICMJE states all rights reserved. Original summaries only; no checklist or full recommendations bundled.

rules.intent: Preserve facts, numbers, units, negation, conditions, exceptions, uncertainty, quotations, citations, and code; distinguish supplied evidence from inference.
rules.rationale: Project-wide meaning-preservation requirement; style never authorizes a factual change.

rules.intent: Use the introduction to establish context, the knowledge gap, and the research question or objective.
rules.rationale: Faithful summary of the selected manuscript-preparation guidance.
exceptions: A review, case report, or other genre may need a different organization.

rules.intent: Describe the actual design, materials/participants, procedures, and analysis sufficiently to interpret and reproduce the work.
rules.rationale: Operational adaptation of methods guidance without study-design-specific completeness claims.
exceptions: Mark missing information or request it; do not invent ethics approval, participants, procedures, or analysis.

rules.intent: Report supplied findings in Results and interpret their implications, limitations, and bounded conclusions in Discussion.
rules.rationale: Faithful summary of IMRaD section roles.
exceptions: The target journal may combine sections; preserve the conceptual distinction even when headings differ.

rules.intent: Check that abstract, methods, results, tables, and discussion agree on quantities, analyses, scope, and uncertainty.
rules.rationale: Project adaptation of manuscript and reporting-guideline consistency review.
exceptions: Use the target journal and appropriate study-design reporting guideline when supplied; their full requirements are not bundled here.
